openbhb.description: Ridge regression of age on frozen features, OpenBHB train split (3,227) to test split (757)

models.name: y-Aware DenseNet-121
models.pretraining: y-Aware contrastive learning on BHB-10K (10,420 volumes of 7,764 healthy participants), with age as proxy
models.input: CAT12 VBM gray matter maps in the MNI space at 1.5 mm, of shape 121 x 145 x 121
models.fidelity: Matches the original implementation. The OpenBHB brain age is optimistic: BHB-10K includes the OpenBHB participants and age was the pretraining proxy.

paper.title: Dufumier et al., Contrastive Learning with Continuous Proxy Meta-Data for 3D MRI Classification, MICCAI 2021

models.name: Neuro-SimCLR ResNet-18
models.pretraining: SimCLR on 44,958 T1w MRI of 18,759 patients from 11 public datasets
models.input: Skull-stripped T1w MRI prepared with TurboPrep, rigidly registered to the MNI152 ICBM 2009c template at 1 mm
models.fidelity: All the weights of the original checkpoint are loaded strictly. OpenBHB images are not prepared with TurboPrep.
models.license: Not stated by the authors (code under MIT)

paper.title: Kaczmarek et al., Building a General SimCLR Self-Supervised Foundation Model Across Neurological Diseases to Advance 3D Brain MRI Diagnoses, ICCV Workshops 2025

models.name: BrainIAC ViT-B
models.pretraining: SimCLR on structural brain MRI of several sequences
models.input: Skull-stripped, bias-corrected MRI, rigidly registered to the BrainIAC template (170 x 206 x 162 at 1 mm, LAS)
models.fidelity: The encoder matches an independent implementation of the original model within 1e-6. nidl averages the patch tokens where the original code returns the first one.
models.license: BrainIAC Research-Only (non-commercial), redistributed with the approval of the authors

paper.title: Tak et al., A generalizable foundation model for analysis of human brain MRI, Nature Neuroscience 2026

models.name: Neuro-JEPA ViT-B
models.pretraining: JEPA on about 1.55 million T1w, T2w and FLAIR scans from NYU Langone Health
models.input: Skull-stripped, bias-corrected MRI, affinely registered to MNI152 at 1 mm
models.fidelity: Features bit-identical to the official code, preprocessing included, on the 3,984 OpenBHB images.

paper.title: Huang et al., Learning Sparse Latent Predictive Foundation Model for Multimodal Neuroimaging, arXiv 2026
